episodes.186329: A kona low developed west-northwest of the Hawaiian Islands and brought periods of heavy rainfall and isolated thunderstorms. Heavy rainfall lead to localized flash flooding and landslides across portions of the State. Impacts from the kona low continued into December 2023 and are covered in episode 186869.
episodes.186384: A warm front lingered near the Interstate 10 corridor in the afternoon with deep, moist and unsettled SW steering flow aloft. With NE FL within the warm sector, a couple of isolated strong to pulse severe storms and locally heavy rainfall impacted NE FL in the afternoon and early evening with gusty winds and minor wind damage.

episodes.186980: Rain showers occurred in southeast Kansas during the day into the overnight hours of the 30th. Heavy rain began to fall around 10PM at the Chanute Airport which coincides with the time of a fatal vehicular accident that occurred nearby.
episodes.187269: Isolated flooding occurred from a slow moving storm in Jefferson County.
episodes.187773: A deepening surface low formed across the ArkLaTex region in the early morning hours on December 1st. In the warm sector of the low, thunderstorms formed along a convergent axis almost parallel to the upper-level flow, which caused training to occur over an urban area (Baton Rouge). That same batch of convection eventually cold-pooled out and raced east when a bowing segment produced a very brief tornado in Pearl River county, aided by a surging rear-inflow jet. After that convection exited the area, another batch formed during the late evening hours, with one cell becoming dominant and producing golf ball sized hail before the whole complex weakened.

events.narrative: Wind gust occurred at the Galveston North Jetty.
Persistent heavy rainfall lead to water accumulating on the roads which prompted the road closure of Wood Valley Road.
Roads were flooded and multiple vehicles were disabled near the TX 124 and Broadway Avenue area of Winnie.

Periods of heavy rainfall lead to an accumulation of water on the roadways which led to the closure of Piilani highway from mile marker 29-31, as well as mile marker 16. Hana Highway was also closed near mile marker 40.
The south fork of Taylor Bayou flooded roadways near Interstate 10 after heavy rain fell|near Hampshire.

Heavy rain was occurring according to the nearby airport observation at Chanute Martin Johnson Airport when a car crossed the center line and hit a semi freightliner head-on. Unfortunately the driver of the car died from this car crash near the intersection of Kansas Highway 39 and Brown Road.
A station in the Olustee Forest measured storm total rainfall of 3.20 inches.
A mesonet site measured 2.41 inches of storm total rainfall.
A mesonet site near Live Oak measured storm total rainfall of 4.68 inches.
A mesonet site near Macclenny measured 4.07 inches of  storm total rainfall.
A mesonet site near Blue Springs measured 2.87 inches of storm total rainfall.
A mesonet station near Statenville measured 2.69 inches of storm total rain.
Heavy rain caused a drainage ditch to overflow covering a few areas with shallow water.
Significant street flooding occurred along Ambassador Caffery Parkway with one vehicle stalled. Most of the flooding occurred from Johnston Road and the Vermilion River.
Hana Highway was closed near mile marker 40. And Piilani Highway was closed near mile marker 16, and 29-31.
Public reported street flooding with road closures. Reported vehicles stranded.

NWS storm survey determined a weak tornado with max estimated winds of 65 mph touched down just south of Jacobs Road. The tornado was briefly on the ground for 1-minute, tracking north for 0.3 miles. The max path width was 75 yards. The tornado knocked down a few trees with a considerable amount of branches snapped in its path. A car port was destroyed, a RV flipped, and a truck rolled.
Picture of large hail estimated to be around golf ball size near Labadieville. Relayed by broadcast media.
